neighbours.label: 'In spite' / 'Despite' opening a concession to the fact stated in the previous sentence (In spite of this, Despite that); peaks on ' spite' / ' Despite'
fire: The engine was forty years old and leaked oil. In spite of this, the boat crossed the bay.
Her mother had warned her twice about the cold. In spite of that, she left her coat at home.
The harvest failed two years in a row. Despite this, the farmers refused to sell their land.
Nobody in the office liked the new schedule. Despite that, it stayed in place all winter.
The museum had lost most of its funding. In spite of this, it opened a new wing in March.
The climbers were short of food and rope. Despite this, they pushed on toward the summit.
His first two novels sold almost nothing. In spite of that, the publisher offered him a contract.
The printer jammed on every third page. Despite that, the report went out on time.
quiet: The engine was forty years old and leaked oil. Because of this, the boat stayed in the harbour.
Her mother had warned her twice about the cold. As a result, she packed two coats.
The harvest failed two years in a row. Because of that, many farmers sold their land.
Nobody in the office liked the new schedule. As a result, it was dropped within a week.
The museum had lost most of its funding. For this reason, it closed its east wing in March.
The climbers were short of food and rope. Thanks to this, they agreed to turn back early.
His first two novels sold almost nothing. Because of this, the publisher let him go.
The printer jammed on every third page. As a result, the report went out late.

notes: A sub-trigger: the top examples also hold verbs before a back-reference ('reflect this shift', 'reduce this number', 'violated that trust'), 'due to' and code tokens before a just-named variable, and the output promotes ' these' / ' this' / ' such'. In probes 'Because of this' read 0.05, so the test claims the concessive opener only.
